name: scale_field
title: Scale-space field on the momentum cohort
not_a_phase: BRIEF.md: 'This is not a phase prompt and does not want to become one.' The method has ~one free parameter, so there is nothing to pre-register. Correctness is enforced by research/scale_field/test_scale_field.py, which is the specification. What is kept from the standard: numbered decisions append-only, the evidence standard, the frozen cohort with its hash asserted, segment stratification, D4, 'the artifact wins'. The moment anything here touches forward returns, the full standard applies again.

cohort.rule: FROZEN. Phase 10 manifest, reused, never redrawn or extended. Hash asserted on every run.
cohort.hard_stop_on_mismatch: reconciliation stop -- the only escalation this brief carries beyond the Allan gate

read_path.rule: ZERO passes over filtered_trades / filtered_quotes. Every tick read is a targeted per-event parquet read, reusing research/phase_10/common.py:read_event_trades unchanged.
read_path.tie_order: sequence_number, ascending; never inverts under the sip sort

analysis_clock.decision: D3 -- extended-day analysis clock, America/New_York, DST-aware
analysis_clock.timezone_rule: segment assignment computed in America/New_York from the pinned XNYS calendar, never by casting the UTC sip_timestamp to a date
analysis_clock.segment_partition_rule: premarket [04:00, rth_open) | rth [rth_open, rth_close) | post [rth_close, post_end). The three tile the extended session exactly and are disjoint; the adapter test asserts it.

segments_not_poolable.rule: premarket and rth are reported separately, never pooled.
segments_not_poolable.evidence: v3 measured 0.903 decades of separation between premarket and regular hours (failure row 5).
segments_not_poolable.note: Two distinct segment notions are in play and are never conflated: the EVENT-level detection segment (det_segment_poll1, where the D7 anchor fell) stratifies events; the PRINT-level segment slices one event's tape by wall clock. The adapter exposes the second; the manifest carries the first.

d4.rule: Tick-derived only. No spine numeric column on any computation path.

reconciliation.rule: allan_factor() must reproduce v3's committed curve rung for rung. HARD STOP on divergence -- any divergence means the point-process handling differs from v3's and everything after it is uninterpretable.
reconciliation.window_origin: the D3 extended session [04:00 ET, post_end); windows tile the full in-window session so empty stretches are real zeros
reconciliation.tolerance_note: Exact float reproduction is the bar, not an approximate one -- both paths run the same arithmetic on the same integers. The tolerance exists only to absorb float association order.
reconciliation.v3_knees_role: A PREDICTION for the continuous field, not an input to it. The scale axis should show a change of character near them. If it does not, one of the two measurements is wrong and that is the finding.

scale_axis.rule: The scale axis is a continuum; these arrays are quadrature for plotting, not a kernel grid in the method.
scale_axis.hard_floor_note: 2^-20 s = 0.954 us, ~12x the 80.5 ns median timestamp resolution (49 ns min). Below it you are measuring quantization.

fine.coverage: +/- 15 s around the D7 detection anchor, read with +/- 15 min of context
fine.why_not_session_wide: > 110 s/event, impractical. The fragmentation scale lives at the fine end and does not need session-wide coverage; the coarse end is cheap and does.
fine.window_deviation_from_brief: THE BRIEF SAYS +/- 15 MIN; THIS RUNS +/- 15 s OF CHARTED WINDOW INSIDE A +/- 15 MIN READ. Recorded, not silently taken. A heatmap column cannot be narrower than its kernel or the panel draws sub-pixel structure as noise. Over 1,800 s a ~1,400-column chart gives 1.3 s per column, against a smallest kernel of 15.6 ms -- so the bottom six octaves of the fine band alias, and the first render duly showed a picket fence. The honest window for a band reaching 15.6 ms is W x 15.6 ms ~ 22 s. At +/- 15 s with 1,500 grid points the spacing is 20 ms, which resolves the floor, and the top scale (1 s) still spans 30 kernel widths. The +/- 15 min of tape is still READ, so the estimator has full context either side and the edge mask never bites inside the charted window. Compute cost is unchanged -- it is set by the pyramid's bin count over the read window, not by the grid -- so the brief's 7 s/event budget still holds.

scale_axis.coarse_cap_rule: session_span / 8. STATED, not silently applied: at s = 4096 s a regular-hours session (~23,400 s) holds ~2 independent windows, which is where v3's headline A = 1,245 sits. The 2048 s ceiling is below the cap for the extended session (57,600/8 = 7,200 s) and below it for RTH alone (23,400/8 = 2,925 s).

field.neff_rule: field() returns NaN under n_eff >= 8 and MUST NEVER be given a fallback. Same treatment as insufficient_context.
field.tie_variant: collapse_same_timestamp -- consecutive prints sharing a timestamp collapse to one arrival (reference variant, config/phase_10_v4.json)
field.t_grid_rule: Grid spacing must be <= the band's smallest scale, or the field is sampled below its own resolution and every chart of it aliases. coarse: 57,600 s / 900 = 64 s per column against a 1 s smallest scale -- the coarse heatmap is therefore ALSO under-sampled at its fine end and is read as a coarse-scale picture only. fine: 30 s / 1,500 = 20 ms against 15.6 ms.

poisson_null.status: UNIT-TEST FIXTURE ONLY. Never a threshold on this data.
poisson_null.why: The constant is exact for a Poisson process and this tape is nowhere near Poisson: Phase 10 v3 measured the Allan factor at 5.99 at T = 15.6 ms rising monotonically to 1,245 at T = 4,096 s. A z-score against Poisson would be inflated by roughly sqrt(A(T)) -- about 2.4x at milliseconds and ~35x at the hour scale.
poisson_null.replacement: Rate-matched inhomogeneous Poisson realisations simulated from each event's own intensity estimate, with that event's duration and timestamp quantisation. Machinery already specified in prompts/phase_10b.md T3c (200 draws, 2.5/97.5 percentile band, reported as a family over the bandwidth rather than one band) and already implemented in research/phase_10b/pipeline.py. REUSE IT; DO NOT REBUILD IT.
poisson_null.gated_on: step 5 of the brief's order of work -- after Cooper reads the single-event chart.

charts.grammar: extends research/phase_10d_diag1/plot_boundary_through_time.py, recorded as reusable for exactly this, with the kernel-scale axis replacing the boundary track

order_of_work: 1. adapter.py, plus a test that loads one known event and asserts monotone, positive, in-session timestamps.
2. Allan reconciliation against v3. HARD STOP on divergence.
3. One event, both bands, both channels. Chart it and STOP.
5. Only then: matched-null thresholds, then the cohort.
forward_returns: NOT TOUCHED. The moment anything here touches forward returns, the full Agent_Prompt_Standard applies again, pre-registered, no exceptions.
